payload.body: ## Pull request overview This PR addresses accessibility and keyboard navigation gaps for Radar visualizations and the Compare flow by adding ARIA labeling, landmark roles, focus-visible styling, and a new a11y-focused test. **Changes:** - Added `/<desc>`, `role`, and `aria-labelledby` enhancements to Radar SVG outputs and the dashboard RadarChart SVG. - Improved keyboard focus visibility and ARIA labeling across CompareClient interactive controls (inputs, buttons, recent items, share/export actions). - Added a new `CompareClient.a11y-keyboard.test.tsx` to validate ARIA labels and focus-visible class presence. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments. <details> <summary>Show a summary per file</summary> | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `lib/svg/radar.ts` | Adds accessible metadata and per-axis dots/tooltips to generated Radar SVG output. | | `components/dashboard/RadarChart.tsx` | Adds region + SVG `role="img"` and `title/desc` for screen readers. | | `app/compare/CompareClient.tsx` | Adds focus-visible styling and aria-label improvements for keyboard navigation. | | `app/compare/CompareClient.a11y-keyboard.test.tsx` | New tests covering ARIA labels and focus-visible class usage. | | `components/burnout/BurnoutRiskTable.tsx` | Type formatting/refactor (no functional behavior change). | </details> --- 💡 <a href="/JhaSourav07/commitpulse/new/main?filename=.github/skills/code-review/SKILL.md" class="Link--inTextBlock" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Add a `code-review` agent skill</a> or configure MCP servers for context-aware, tailored reviews. <a href="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/request-a-code-review/use-code-review#mcp-servers-and-agent-skills" class="Link--inTextBlock" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Learn more in the docs.</a>

payload.title: Fix Architecture: Convert getDirSize to Async with Early Exit to Prevent Timeout

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Excellent architectural fix! Converting \getDirSize\ to be fully asynchronous in \oute.ts\ is crucial for serverless environments to prevent blocking the event loop on large repositories. The early exit condition \if (totalSize > limit)\ is a brilliant optimization that will save significant execution time when users accidentally submit massive repos. Additionally, skipping the \.git\ directory entirely is a very smart move since we don't care about git history size for the architecture analysis.

The tests added to \oute.test.ts\ perfectly validate both the \.git\ exclusion and the early-exit behavior.

Labels applied:
- **type:performance**: Greatly optimizes disk I/O and prevents serverless timeouts on large clones.
- **level:intermediate**: Requires careful handling of recursive async filesystem traversal and short-circuiting.
- **quality:exceptional**: Clean, efficient code with robust and specific test cases.

## Pull request overview This PR extends the `/customize` GitHub background preview simulator from a 2-state dark/light toggle to a 3-mode selector (Dark / Light / Checkerboard) and wires the same control into `ExportPanel` so users can validate transparency while reviewing export snippets. **Changes:** - Introduces a reusable `PreviewBackgroundMode` type (`'dark' | 'light' | 'checkerboard'`). - Replaces the Live Preview background toggle with a 3-button simulator and adds checkerboard styling to the preview container. - Adds optional `previewBg` / `onPreviewBgChange` props to `ExportPanel` + new unit tests for the simulator buttons. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 7 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | app/customize/types.ts | Adds `PreviewBackgroundMode` type for consistent background-mode typing. | | app/customize/page.tsx | Updates Live Preview UI to a 3-mode background simulator and passes mode state into `ExportPanel`. | | app/customize/components/ExportPanel.tsx | Adds an optional background simulator control group to the export header controls. | | app/customize/components/ExportPanel.bg-simulator.test.tsx | Adds tests verifying simulator rendering and click behavior. |
Suppressed comments (7) **app/customize/page.tsx:577** * The Dark button is missing a descriptive accessible label beyond the visible text. Adding an `aria-label` also keeps existing tests (which query for “switch to … background preview”) stable after moving from a single toggle to a button group. ``` ``` **app/customize/page.tsx:592** * The Light button should have a descriptive `aria-label` (action-oriented) rather than relying only on the short visible text. This also keeps the existing CustomizePage preview background tests stable (they look for “switch to light background preview”). ``` ``` **app/customize/page.tsx:614** * The Grid button label is hard-coded; for consistency with the rest of the localized UI, route this through `t(...)` with a `defaultValue`. ``` Grid ``` **app/customize/components/ExportPanel.tsx:410** * This user-facing label is hard-coded; for consistency with the rest of ExportPanel's localized strings, wrap it with `t(...)` (using `defaultValue` so it works even if the key isn't present yet). ``` Light ``` **app/customize/components/ExportPanel.tsx:424** * This user-facing label is hard-coded; ExportPanel is otherwise localized via `t(...)`. Consider wrapping it in `t(...)` with a `defaultValue` to avoid mixed-language UI. ```

payload.body:
## Pull request overview Adds first-class Docker support so CommitPulse can be run and deployed in containers (including a local MongoDB via Compose), aligning with the self-hosting goals in #8284. **Changes:** - Document Docker-based workflows in `README.md` (Compose for local runs + `docker build/run` for production). - Enable Next.js standalone output to support slimmer runtime images. - Add Docker artifacts: `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, and `.dockerignore`. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | README.md | Adds Docker usage documentation for local and production container runs. | | next.config.ts | Enables `output: 'standalone'` so Next builds can be packaged into a smaller runtime image. | | Dockerfile | Introduces a multi-stage build that runs a Next standalone server in production. | | docker-compose.yml | Defines an app service plus a MongoDB service for containerized local runs. | | .dockerignore | Reduces Docker build context size and avoids copying local env files into builds. |
--- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body: I appreciate you looking into improving the clipboard fallback in \utils/clipboard.ts\. However, I have a concern with the changes: the \.select()\ method on \HTMLTextAreaElement\ returns \oid\ (undefined), not a boolean indicating success. Because of this, \const selected = textArea.select(); if (!selected) return false;\ will always evaluate to false and the function will never reach \execCommand('copy')\. Please double-check the MDN documentation for \HTMLTextAreaElement.select()\ and revise this approach. I'll have to request changes for now.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
\HTMLTextAreaElement.select()\ actually returns \oid\ (undefined), not a boolean indicating success. This means \!selected\ will always evaluate to true, and your fallback copy function will *always* return false without ever attempting to execute the copy command. 

Please revise this. The correct way to handle selection fallback is to use a \	ry...catch\ block around \document.execCommand('copy')\, which you already have. You do not need to check the return value of \select()\. I am requesting changes because this breaks the fallback clipboard entirely.

Labels applied:
- **type:bug**: An attempted fix that introduces a new failure condition.
- **level:beginner**: Involves standard DOM API return types.

payload.author: ChetanSenta
payload.title: Fix PDF Export Image Load Watchdog Timer

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body:
## Pull request overview This PR fixes a resource-cleanup gap in `exportSvgToPdf()` by ensuring the 5-second image-load watchdog timer is cleared when the image load either succeeds or fails, preventing dangling timers after PDF exports. **Changes:** - Capture the watchdog `setTimeout` handle and `clearTimeout()` it in both `image.onload` and `image.onerror`. - Add a regression test to verify the image-load timeout is cleared on successful load. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 1 comment. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | lib/pdf-export.ts | Captures and clears the image-load watchdog timeout on both load success and failure paths. | | lib/pdf-export.test.ts | Adds a regression test around timeout cleanup behavior during PDF export. |
Suppressed comments (1) **lib/pdf-export.test.ts:199** * Restore both spies and assert `clearTimeout` was invoked with the specific timeout handle returned by `setTimeout`, rather than only asserting it was called. ``` expect(clearTimeoutSpy).toHaveBeenCalled(); clearTimeoutSpy.mockRestore(); }); ```
--- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body: Excellent cleanup! Leaving dangling timeouts can definitely lead to subtle memory leaks or unexpected behavior in long-running processes. Capturing the \	imeoutId\ and clearing it on both success and error in \lib/pdf-export.ts\ is the textbook correct way to handle this. The mock image test is also well done. Approved!

payload.author: ChetanSenta
payload.title: fix(spotify): correct SVG generation by truncating before escaping

payload.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
payload.body:
## Pull request overview This PR fixes malformed Spotify SVG/XML generation by changing `generateSpotifySVG()` to truncate raw track title/artist strings *before* XML-escaping them, preventing truncation from splitting multi-character XML entities (e.g. `&`) into invalid fragments. **Changes:** - Update `generateSpotifySVG()` to truncate raw title/artist first, then apply `escapeXML()`. - Add a Vitest regression test suite intended to validate the truncation-before-escaping behavior. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | lib/svg/spotify.ts | Adjusts truncation/escaping order to prevent broken XML entities in rendered `` nodes. | | lib/svg/spotify.test.ts | Adds regression tests for the truncation-before-escaping fix (with some test corrections needed). |
Suppressed comments (1) **lib/svg/spotify.test.ts:30** * After introducing `defaultParams`, the second test can also use it instead of casting a partial object to SpotifyParams. This keeps the test consistent with the rest of the SVG generator tests that call `*.parse({})` for defaults. ``` const params: SpotifyParams = { width: 400, height: 150 } as SpotifyParams; ```
--- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

This PR is currently blocked because of failing CI checks. By changing the hashing mechanism to \ crypt\ (\lib/notification-management-token.ts\), the generated hashes are no longer deterministic (since \ crypt\ automatically generates a random salt) and they do not output a 64-character hex string. This breaks our existing test assertions in \lib/notification-management-token.test.ts\.

**How to fix:**
Please update the test assertions to remove the \^[a-f0-9]{64}$\ regex check, and remove the determinism test (\eturns a deterministic hash for the same input\). Also, since bcrypt hashes are non-deterministic, you will need to update the token verification logic (wherever this hash is compared) to use \ crypt.compareSync()\ instead of simple string equality.

I am requesting changes until the CI is green.

payload.body: ## Pull request overview Improves GitHub API resiliency by adjusting retry/abort behavior and contribution-request coalescing to reduce duplicated calls and avoid leaking sensitive request details, while also tweaking CI analytics paging and reordering the socials registry. **Changes:** - Updates `fetchWithRetry` error/abort handling and adjusts contribution-fetch coalescing so abort signals don’t bypass deduplication. - Reduces CI Actions pagination depth for CI analytics fetches. - Sorts the socials registry alphabetically at module initialization. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 3 out of 3 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | services/github/ci-analytics.ts | Reduces Actions pagination (likely to lower API usage). | | lib/github.ts | Changes abort/error behavior in retry logic and contribution request coalescing for better dedup + safer error surfaces. | | app/generator/data/socials.ts | Sorts socials registry by display name (user-visible ordering change). | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
This is a solid improvement to our GraphQL rate limit handling and request cancellation logic! The way you're handling \AbortError\ and coalescing requests is very robust.

However, similar to PR #8274, it looks like this branch contains unrelated changes that were accidentally committed. Specifically, the changes to \pp/generator/data/socials.ts\ and \services/github/ci-analytics.ts\ do not belong in this PR.

To fix this, please revert the changes to those files using \git restore\ or \git checkout\ so that this PR is focused entirely on the GitHub API rate limit and token handling.

Looking forward to getting this merged once the branch is cleaned up!

**Label Justification:**
- \level:advanced\: Implementing complex request coalescing, abort controller logic, and rate-limit backoff across the API layer is an advanced task.
- \	ype:bug\ & \	ype:security\: Prevents token exhaustion and handles API edge cases securely.
- \mentor:Aamod007\: Assigned as required.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
New commits address some of the previous concerns. The signal/abort refactoring in `fetchGitHubContributions` looks notably better — properly propagating abort signals through the coalesced promise pattern rather than ignoring them. The error message extraction (`fetchError instanceof Error ? fetchError.message : String(fetchError)`) is a good improvement too.

CI is still failing though. Please check the logs and fix whatever is causing the failures before we can approve.

Label justification:
- level:advanced — the async signal propagation + coalesced promise pattern is non-trivial, spans 4 files including github.ts which has complex retry/abort logic
- quality:clean — well-structured changes
- type:bug, type:security — rate limit error handling + token security
- mentor:Aamod007 — assigned

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Thanks for looking into this styling issue on the support page! 

However, completely removing the \ ixed\ class from the \<nav>\ is not the best approach here, as it breaks the sticky behavior of the navbar when the user scrolls down the page. The standard way to fix content overlapping a \ ixed\ navbar is to add adequate padding (like \pt-20\ or similar) to the top of the main content container (\<main>\ or the next \<div>\) so it sits below the navbar. 

Additionally, using \mr-10\ on the Discord button feels a bit like a workaround. Consider using flexbox gap properties on the parent container if you're trying to separate it from adjacent elements. 

Please restore the \ ixed\ class and apply top padding to the main content instead. 

**Label Justification:**
- \level:beginner\: CSS padding/margin and positioning fixes fall under beginner-level styling tasks.
- \	ype:bug\: Fixes layout overlap.
- \	ype:design\: Modifies UI layout and spacing.
- \mentor:Aamod007\: Assigned as required.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Thanks for implementing this request deduplication! This will definitely help reduce API usage and rate limits. 

However, there is a critical bug in the implementation: \dedupeRequest\ caches and shares the \Promise<Response>\ across multiple callers. Since a \Response\ body (e.g., via \es.json()\) can only be consumed once, any concurrent caller trying to read the body of the shared response object will encounter a 'body stream already read' error. To fix this, the deduplication layer needs to either cache the parsed JSON data instead of the \Response\ object, or explicitly call \es.clone()\ for each subsequent consumer. 

Also, it looks like this PR needs a rebase as it has conflicts with the \main\ branch. Please rebase and fix the response consumption issue so we can get this merged!

**Label Justification:**
- \level:advanced\: Implementing concurrency control and request deduplication requires a deep understanding of asynchronous JavaScript and the Fetch API's Response lifecycle.
- \quality:clean\: The utility structure is cleanly written.
- \	ype:performance\: Directly optimizes network requests.
- \mentor:Aamod007\: Assigned as required.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Thank you for adding these comprehensive timezone boundary tests! Validating the cooldown gate across different local times is a great idea.

However, the CI checks are failing (\Format · Lint · Typecheck · Test\). The likely culprit here is that dynamically reassigning \process.env.TZ = tz;\ in the middle of a Node.js process (which Vitest uses) does not reliably update the runtime's timezone for standard \Date\ APIs. If a test relies on the global timezone shifting mid-suite, it will likely fail. To test different timezones reliably, you either need to pass the \	imeZone\ option into the \Intl\ formats explicitly (which you did in some tests!), or use a mocking library that can spoof the system timezone. 

Please check the GitHub Actions logs to see the exact failure, adjust the tests to pass, and we can get this merged!

**Label Justification:**
- \level:beginner\: Writing standard unit tests using Vitest and React Testing Library is a foundational task.
- \quality:clean\: Applied as default for clean test code.
- \	ype:testing\: Focuses purely on expanding test coverage.
- \mentor:Aamod007\: Assigned as required.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Nice work on the mock integration tests for DescriptionSection. You've correctly identified that this component has no async service calls or loading states, and rather than fabricating tests for non-existent behaviors, you focused on what actually exists: prop flow, the SectionCard/FieldLabel mock integration, onChange callback behavior, and the character limit counter. That's the right call.

A few small things I noticed while reading through DescriptionSection.mock-integrations.test.tsx:

The FieldLabel mock is defined inside the SectionCard module mock (i.mock('../SectionCard', ...)), which is correct since they're co-located in the same module. Good structural awareness there.

The character limit test at line ~60 asserts '262 characters remaining' against a value of 'Frontend developer' — that's pinned to a specific character budget. Worth a quick comment in the test explaining where that 280-character limit comes from, just so future contributors don't wonder why 262 and not some other number.

Overall this is clean, purposeful test coverage that respects the actual component contract. level:intermediate fits well — the mock wiring and prop-flow verification required real judgment about what to test.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
I can see what you were trying to do here, and extracting a STREAK_CACHE_CONTROL constant from pp/api/streak/cache.ts is a reasonable idea in principle. But the way it's applied in the test changes actually *weakens* the existing test coverage, which is a problem.

In oute.test.ts, the original test at line ~457 was:
`	s
expect(response.headers.get('Cache-Control')).toBe(
  'public, max-age=60, s-maxage=3600, stale-while-revalidate=59'
);
`

Your change replaces this with:
`	s
expect(response.headers.get('Cache-Control')).toBe(STREAK_CACHE_CONTROL);
`

Where STREAK_CACHE_CONTROL = 'public, max-age=60, s-maxage=1, stale-while-revalidate=59'.

Notice what happened: the s-maxage changed from 3600 to 1. This means either (a) the original test was wrong and there's a bug in the application, or (b) you changed the expected value to match a constant you defined rather than what the route actually produces. The second test case 'reflects a different time value when the clock changes' had s-maxage=7200 originally, but your constant forces it to s-maxage=1 — which eliminates the point of that test entirely.

In oute.timezone-boundaries.test.ts, the same problem occurs: expect(response.headers.get('Cache-Control')).toContain('s-maxage=7200') was replaced with a fixed constant that has s-maxage=1. Those tests existed to verify that the route correctly picks up the timezone-aware TTL from getSecondsUntilMidnightInTimezone. Replacing them with a static constant means the mock return value no longer matters.

Please revert the test changes to use the concrete expected strings rather than the constant. If you want to extract the constant for use in production code that's fine, but test assertions should pin the exact values the route is expected to produce.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Good refactor of AIRecommendationsPanel. Moving from index-based keys to item.id or item.title keys in the recommendation list is exactly the right fix — index-based keys cause React to re-render unnecessarily and lose component state during list reorders.

The animation cleanup is also solid: wrapping individual items in motion containers with staggered delay props is better than applying a blanket animation to the container. The code in the component reads cleanly.

One thing to check: if item.id is not guaranteed to be unique across the recommendations array (or if it's undefined for some items), you might still fall back to unstable keys. Worth adding a quick sanity check that the data source always provides unique, stable IDs before considering this fully resolved.

Overall this is a clean, purposeful refactor that improves render stability. level:intermediate fits — it requires understanding React reconciliation to know why key stability matters.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
This is a solid improvement to the ErrorBoundary test setup. The key changes you made are all good calls:

Switching from Object.defineProperty(navigator, 'clipboard', ...) to i.stubGlobal('navigator', ...) is cleaner and avoids the configurable/writable descriptor gymnastics that can cause cross-test pollution. Extracting mockWriteText as a shared reference also makes it easier to assert on calls if needed.

Moving the import ErrorBoundary from './error' to after the i.mock() calls fixes the hoisting issue — in Vitest, mocks need to be established before the module is imported for them to intercept correctly.

Replacing  ireEvent with userEvent for interactive elements is the right ergonomic choice, though I notice you actually went the other direction in some places (replacing userEvent with  ireEvent). For simple click interactions that's fine, but for typing scenarios userEvent is generally preferred.

The status:blocked label indicates CI is failing — worth checking whether the test runner actually passes locally after these changes, since the i.stubGlobal approach may behave differently in some environments. Once CI is green this is ready to go.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
The new test file pp/api/student/resume/confirm/route.timezone-boundaries.test.ts has two serious problems.

First, there's a garbled character at the top of the file: ???import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';. That leading ??? would cause a syntax error. The file as-is wouldn't even parse.

Second, and more importantly, the tests import 
ormalizeTimezone,  ormatDateForLocale, isValidDate, and handleDST from './route' — but the student resume confirm route handler doesn't export any of these functions. They simply don't exist in that file. Every test in this suite would fail with a runtime import error, not because of a logic bug, but because the functions being tested don't exist in the targeted module.

If you want to add timezone utility tests, they should either target an actual utility module that exports those functions (like utils/time.ts), or if these utilities need to be added to the confirm route, they need to actually be implemented and exported there first. As it stands, this PR is importing and testing non-existent exports.

For the lib/svg/themes.ts change adding sanitizeHexColor and updating the  adgeThemeSchema to accept #-prefixed hex values — that part looks like a reasonable feature. But it's bundled with the broken test file, so the whole PR needs to be cleaned up before it can merge.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body: @SahilSolve02 Hey, I took a look at your PR #7956 and the 8 CI failures. The root issue is that your change wraps the fetch logic in a try-catch and returns HTTP 200 with an SVG error card for invalid usernames, but the existing test suite expects specific error status codes — 404 for not-found users, 429 for rate limits, 500 for server errors — along with matching cache headers like no-cache and no-store. When you return 200 instead, all those assertions break. The good news is the codebase already handles this exactly the way the issue describes. If you look at route.ts around lines 841-857, there's already a generateNotFoundSVG() call that returns a friendly SVG error card with a 404 status. The reason it uses 404 and not 200 is intentional — since these SVGs are embedded in READMEs via tags, the browser renders the SVG body regardless of the HTTP status code, so the user still sees the nice error card. But keeping the proper status code prevents CDNs from caching the error as if it were a successful response, which would mean the error gets stuck and never retries. So the fix is to not change the status codes or cache headers at all. If the SVG error card itself needs a design update (like making it darker or changing the text), that should be done inside generateNotFoundSVG() in lib/svg/generator.ts. I'd also recommend running npx vitest run app/api/streak/route.test.ts locally before pushing — that'll catch these failures immediately.

payload.author: Aamod007
payload.body:
Solid regression fix for the streak grace period bug. The core issue you identified is real: the dead-code assignment 	odayIndex = lastIndex inside lib/calculate.ts was overwriting the gap check result, which meant the grace period limit was never actually enforced. Removing that line is the right fix.

The new test file lib/calculate.grace-period.test.ts does what regression tests should do — it pins the broken behavior as something that must not regress. The  uildCalendarEndingDaysAgo helper is clean and the two cases (gap exceeds grace period → reset to 0, gap within grace period → streak survives) directly target the bug.

The changes to lib/calculate.test.ts are also thoughtful: the new 	odayFor() helper fixes a pre-existing issue where tests relied on the system clock, making them time-dependent. Pinning 
ow explicitly is the correct approach and I can see you explained the reasoning in the JSDoc comment above the function.

The commented-out test at line ~548 (// it('does not walk past the start of a 1-day calendar...')) should be cleaned up — either remove it or uncomment and fix it. Leaving dead commented code in tests adds noise.

payload.author: atul-upadhyay-7
payload.body:
@Aamod007 Thanks for the review! I've addressed the empty diff issue by recreating the webhook route with proper event processing.

**What was wrong:**
The legacy `/api/webhook` route was deleted during a merge conflict resolution, leaving the PR with 0 files changed.

**Changes made:**
1. ✅ **Recreated `app/api/webhook/route.ts`** — Full webhook processing pipeline:
   - Rate limiting (10 requests/60s per IP)
   - GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET validation
   - HMAC-SHA256 signature verification (timing-safe comparison)
   - Payload size validation (1MB limit)
   - Event parsing via `parseWebhookEvent`
   - Event caching via `cacheEvent` for analytics
   - Alert evaluation via `evaluateAlerts` for CI/CD notifications
   - Proper error handling and logging

2. ✅ **Added `app/api/webhook/route.test.ts`** — 10 tests covering:
   - Signature verification (missing, invalid, valid)
   - Payload validation (empty body, invalid JSON)
   - Rate limiting
   - CI/CD event processing
   - Non-CI/CD event acknowledgment
   - Error handling

**Validation results:**
- ✅ All 10 tests pass
- ✅ Format clean
- ✅ 367 lines added

Ready for re-review! 🙏
